title: Streamline manifest transcoder and tokenizer sync
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Refactor the model loading pipeline to introduce a streaming manifest transcoder (manifest.v2), a lazy shard publisher and a tokenizer synchronization handshake. This reduces startup latency and memory during model activation while keeping backwards compatibility with legacy .bin weight bundles. The work includes a small dependency upgrade (protobuf), a compatibility shim for older checkpoint formats, expanded test coverage, and observability improvements for manifest/ shard activation phases.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime can load models using manifest.v2 (streaming) and legacy .bin bundles without manual conversion
Startup 95th-percentile model activation latency reduced by >=20% on 7B workload compared to baseline
Tokenizer sync handshake prevents token-lookup races and reduces tokenization-related load failures to 0 in canary
Unit and integration tests covering translation, lazy publish, and tokenizer epoch handshake added and green in CI
Feature-flagged rollout path exists and can be toggled per-customer/account
Observability panels show manifest parsing time, shard activation latency, and cache hit/miss rates
implementation_notes: Introduce StreamManifestTranscoder component that reads incoming manifests and emits incremental shard descriptors for lazy activation
Add compatibility translator that recognizes legacy .bin bundles and produces an on-the-fly manifest view without full conversion to disk
Implement TokenizerEpoch handshake: loader publishes epoch id, tokenizer verifies lexicon hash before allowing KV cache binding
Upgrade protobuf dependency to 3.21.x to support new manifest message shapes; maintain a thin proto-compat layer for older clients
Expose metrics: manifest_parse_ms, shard_activation_ms, tokenizer_epoch_mismatch_count, manifest_translation_bytes
Keep change behind feature flag ingest.experimental.manifest_v2 with canary config in console
tests: Unit: manifest->descriptor translation tests with randomized field order
Integration: end-to-end model load from S3-like store using translator and lazy shard publisher
Stress: concurrent starts with shared sharded weights to validate locking and memory bounds
Fuzz: corrupted manifest variants to ensure translator is resilient and fails fast
Regression: run existing loader smoke tests against compatibility shim for 3 legacy models
rollout_plan: Stage 1: Internal dev clusters with feature flag on (2 days) - smoke and regression runs
Stage 2: Canary customers / 5% traffic on Dedicated pools (72 hours) - monitor shard_activation_ms and error budgets
Stage 3: 25% rollout if canary stable for 72 hours, otherwise rollback to flag-off and triage
Stage 4: Full rollout with automatic fallback policies for tokenizer epoch mismatches
Rollback criteria: >5% increase in activation errors or >10% regression in 95th latency compared to base
risks: Added complexity in boot path increases maintenance burden if translator logic overfits to current manifests
Proto upgrade may interact with other services; proto-compat shim must be thoroughly validated
Tokenizer handshake could introduce small additional hops; ensure handshake cost is amortized by reduced retries
Feature-flag fragmentation risk (multiple flags across teams) - coordinate with infra and console owners
